title: How to apply for a digital nomad visa in Portugal
summary: Live like a local, earn as a foreigner. Master the steps involved in applying for a digital nomad visa in Europe’s oldest nation state — Portugal.
body_markdown:
Did you know that Portugal is the[oldest nation state in Europe](https://eurydice.eacea.ec.europa.eu/national-education-systems/portugal/historical-development#:~:text=Portugal%20is%20the%20oldest%20nation-state%20in%20Europe) ? It's also an attractive destination for digital nomads. Following the rise of remote work, Portugal launched the Digital Nomad (D8) Visa, specifically designed to accommodate those who wish to work remotely. In this article, we’ll guide you through everything you need to know to apply for the Portugal[Digital Nomad Visa](https://grey.co/blog/digital-nomad-visa-countries) in 2024.


## What is the Portugal digital nomad visa?


The *Portugal Digital nomad visa* is part of the broader D8 visa category for people who wish to work remotely while living in Portugal. Remote workers can live in Portugal for up to one year, with the possibility of renewal. You can also transition into residency for a longer-term stay. Popular for its excellent quality of life and solid infrastructure, Portugal has since become one of the favourite destinations for[digital nomads](https://grey.co/blog/top-5-underrated-digital-nomad-visa-destinations) looking for a balanced work-life experience.


### Benefits of living in Portugal as a digital nomad


**Lower cost of living** : Compared to other Western European countries, Portugal offers an affordable lifestyle, especially in areas like Porto or the Algarve. On average, a single person’s monthly expenses can be as low as €1,200, while a small family may spend around €3,000.


**Easy travel access** : Portugal’s strategic location makes it ideal for exploring other parts of Europe. You can easily hop on a flight and visit neighbouring countries, making it an ideal base for those who love to travel.


**Community and networking** : The digital nomad community is growing, particularly in cities like Lisbon and Porto, where you’ll find plenty of co-working spaces, cafés with strong Wi-Fi, and networking opportunities.


**Great climate** : Portugal enjoys a Mediterranean climate, meaning plenty of sunshine year-round, especially in southern regions like the Algarve.


### What are the requirements for the Portugal digital nomad visa?


Before applying for the Portugal Digital Nomad Visa, it’s important to ensure that you meet the eligibility requirements. Here’s a breakdown of the essential criteria:


- **Valid passport** : Your passport should be valid for at least six months beyond your intended stay in Portugal.
- **Remote work employment contract** : You must provide proof that you work for a company based outside of Portugal or that you are self-employed with foreign clients.
- **Proof of income** : You’ll need to show that you have a stable income of at least €2,800 per month, which is four times the minimum wage in Portugal.
- **Health insurance** : You must have valid health insurance that covers you for the duration of your stay.
- **Clean criminal record** : A certificate proving you have no criminal background is required for this visa.
- **Proof of accommodation** : Evidence of where you’ll be staying in Portugal is also required.


These documents are crucial for a successful application, so it’s essential to have everything ready before you begin the process.

### How to apply for the Portugal digital nomad visa


Applying for the Portugal digital nomad visa is straightforward and can be done in a few key steps. Here’s a guide to walk you through the process:


### 1. Gather required documents


Before starting your application, ensure you’ve gathered all the necessary documents:


- A valid passport
- Proof of remote work or freelance employment
- Bank statements showing that you meet the income threshold of €2,800 per month
- Health insurance coverage
- Criminal record certificate
- Proof of accommodation


It’s crucial to double-check each document to avoid errors, as missing paperwork is one of the common reasons for application delays.


### 2. Submit your application online


Once all your documents are ready, head to the[Portuguese Immigration and Borders Service (SEF)](https://imigrante.sef.pt/en/) website to begin your application. You’ll need to fill out the visa application form and upload the relevant documents. The application fee is approximately €100, but this may vary depending on your nationality and location.


### 3. Book an appointment at your local Portuguese consulate


After submitting your application online, you’ll need to book an appointment at your local Portuguese consulate or embassy to complete the process. During this appointment, you’ll be asked to provide biometric data (fingerprints and a photo), and you may be asked some follow-up questions about your application.


### 4. Await approval


Once your application has been submitted and reviewed, you’ll have to wait for the official decision. The processing time varies but generally takes around 60 days. During this period, make sure you keep track of your application status and check if any additional documentation is required.


### 5. Travel to Portugal


Once your visa is approved, you’ll have 90 days to enter Portugal. After arriving, you may apply for a *residence permit* , which will allow you to stay in Portugal for longer than one year.

### Living in Portugal as a digital nomad


Once you’ve secured your visa, it’s time to enjoy life in Portugal. Here are a few tips to help you settle in:


- **Explore co-working spaces** : Cities like[Lisbon and Porto have many co-working spaces](https://grey.co/blog/affordable-european-cities-for-digital-nomads-in-2024) , such as Second Home and Impact Hub, where you can work productively and meet like-minded digital nomads.
- **Stay connected** : Portugal has excellent internet infrastructure, so you won’t need to worry about poor connectivity when working remotely.
- **Learn the basics of Portuguese** : Although many locals speak English, learning basic Portuguese phrases will help you integrate more smoothly into the community.


Applying for the Portugal Digital Nomad Visa is a great way to experience life in one of Europe’s most beautiful and welcoming countries. If you’re ready to start, gather your documents, follow the application process, and enjoy your time working remotely from Portugal.
